findings.title: Credential Theft Infrastructure — RDP Lateral Movement + Privilege Escalation + SAM Dump

peirce_chain.firstness: Event 528: tdungan RDP logon from FALCONIII (10.3.98.10) to WKS-WINXP32BIT via RDP-Tcp#9 at 18:20:21 EST. Logon type 10 (RemoteInteractive). Event 576: SeDebugPrivilege + SeBackupPrivilege + SeRestorePrivilege assigned at same logon timestamp. Event 560/562: Two sequential SAM_SERVER object open/close sequences via lsass.exe PID 1076 at 20:50:21 EST. Handle IDs 882888 and 955648. Access mask 0x62835816.
peirce_chain.secondness: RDP lateral movement from a non-primary workstation (FALCONIII) after hours is atypical for routine work. SeDebugPrivilege enables LSASS memory read and is the canonical prerequisite for mimikatz/pwdump/gsecdump. SeBackupPrivilege allows SAM hive access bypassing ACLs. The combination of these three privileges at logon is a textbook credential theft preparation. 150-minute delay between privilege assignment (18:20) and SAM dump (20:50) suggests deliberate temporal spacing to evade real-time SIEM correlation. Two independent SAM_SERVER handles opened in the same second via lsass is consistent with programmatic SAM enumeration, not manual access. 8/8 habit incongruence anomalies, 99% compromise probability.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Timothy Dungan executed a coordinated credential theft operation: (1) RDP lateral movement from FALCONIII to target workstation after hours, (2) SeDebugPrivilege + SeBackupPrivilege obtained at logon to enable credential access, (3) 150-minute deliberate delay to evade real-time monitoring, (4) SAM credential dump via lsass.exe with two handle operations in the same second. The 150-minute gap is the key intentionality marker — an automated tool would execute immediately; a deliberate operator spaces the attack to avoid temporal correlation. This is active concealment of credential theft: the attacker is hiding the relationship between privilege acquisition and credential dump.

findings.carnegie_pattern: Temporal separation as concealment — deliberately spacing privilege escalation and exploitation to defeat correlation-based detection
findings.devil_advocate: Privileged token assignments (SeDebugPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege) are standard domain policy for IT staff and domain administrators. SAM_SERVER access is a routine LSASS operation during Group Policy refresh or authentication provider initialization. The 150-minute gap could reflect normal work activity between logon and a routine system operation. REFUTATION: (1) SeDebugPrivilege is NOT standard for non-IT employees — it requires explicit Group Policy assignment and is a known attack prerequisite. (2) Two independent SAM_SERVER handles in the same second is NOT Group Policy refresh — it is programmatic enumeration. (3) The 150-minute gap from privilege assignment to SAM dump, combined with after-hours RDP from a non-primary workstation, establishes a deliberate pattern inconsistent with routine system administration. (4) 8/8 habit incongruence anomalies at 99% compromise probability. (5) APT1 IOC confirmed in Redline analysis. Benign hypothesis fails on structural tests.
findings.corroboration: ART-004 (Dropbox + password ZIP) confirms exfiltration staging in same session. ART-005 (APT1 IOC + Gmail) confirms external communication channel.

human_jitter.note: High jitter confirms human insider, not automated tool. Supports insider threat hypothesis.

findings.title: AV Evasion + Pre-Staged Cloud Exfiltration Channel

peirce_chain.firstness: McAfee Failure Audit 257: password-protected 2011-W2.zip containing 2011-W2.pdf blocked AV engine 5400.1158 (DAT 6498.0000) at 20:28:17 EST. Dropbox shell extension created in tdungan profile at 18:20:26 EST — 5 seconds after RDP logon at 18:20:21.
peirce_chain.secondness: Password-protected ZIP blocks AV content inspection — a documented APT1 TTP for evading endpoint detection (T1562.001). The file is named '2011-W2' to mimic a tax form (W-2), providing plausible deniability. Dropbox initialized 5 seconds after RDP logon indicates the exfiltration channel was the first action after establishing lateral access — not an afterthought. The timing correlation (5 seconds) between RDP logon and Dropbox creation is too tight for coincidence.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Deliberate AV evasion via encrypted archive combined with pre-staged cloud exfiltration. The actor: (1) named the ZIP to mimic a tax document for plausible deniability, (2) password-protected it specifically to block AV scanning, (3) initialized Dropbox as the first action of the RDP session for passive exfiltration. This demonstrates operational planning: the exfiltration channel was ready before the credential dump was executed.

findings.carnegie_pattern: Social proof via naming — '2011-W2.zip' mimics legitimate tax document to suppress analyst scrutiny
mitre_ttps: T1048.002 (Exfiltration Over Asymmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol)
findings.devil_advocate: The password-protected ZIP could genuinely be a personal tax document (W-2). Employees routinely store tax documents on work machines. Dropbox is a standard productivity tool initialized at logon by shell integration. PARTIAL ACCEPTANCE: The '2011-W2' naming IS consistent with a legitimate tax document. However: (1) McAfee specifically flagged this file — it was not a routine scan but a failure audit event. (2) Dropbox creation at +5 seconds from RDP logon indicates deliberate initialization, not background shell integration (which would appear at OS boot, not at RDP session start). (3) The temporal sequence — Dropbox first, then credential dump, then AV-evading archive — forms a coherent exfiltration workflow. Verdict maintained at INTENT, not MALICE, because the W-2 naming provides partial plausible deniability that cannot be fully refuted without examining the ZIP contents.
findings.corroboration: ART-001 (RDP lateral movement) confirms the session context. ART-003 (SAM dump) confirms credential theft in the same session.

findings.title: Network Anomalies + Personal Email Channel + APT1 IOC Confirmation

peirce_chain.firstness: TermDD Event 50: WARNING Device\Termdd DATA ENCRYPTION at 20:05:39 EST during active RDP session. Firefox history: Gmail (dungantimothy@gmail.com, 7 inbox messages) accessed at 19:13:48 EST. APT1 IOC match confirmed in Redline .mans analysis.
peirce_chain.secondness: TermDD DATA ENCRYPTION warning indicates RDP cipher negotiation failure or downgrade — consistent with RDP interception, non-standard client, or man-in-the-middle. Gmail access from a corporate host during an active credential theft session creates an exfiltration channel via personal email. The APT1 IOC match in Redline confirms this workstation was targeted by APT1 infrastructure. However, TermDD Event 50 can also indicate routine NLA negotiation issues on Windows XP, and personal email access is common (though ill-advised).
peirce_chain.thirdness: Three signals within one artifact suggest the RDP session was compromised or non-standard, personal email was used as a communication/exfiltration channel, and APT1 infrastructure targeted this workstation. However, each signal individually has benign explanations, and this is a single-source finding. Rated SUSPICION per Daubert single-source standard.

findings.devil_advocate: TermDD Event 50 is common on Windows XP with NLA negotiation — it does not necessarily indicate interception. Gmail access is routine personal email usage. APT1 IOC match requires further .mans extraction to confirm scope. PARTIAL ACCEPTANCE: Each signal individually has plausible benign explanations. The combination is suspicious but does not reach INTENT without a second independent artifact. Downgraded to SUSPICION.
findings.corroboration: Single source. No second artifact independently confirms TermDD anomaly or Gmail exfiltration function.
